- **The osban's broth is the couscous's steam — the two-story's marriage, run on the celebration's own pot.** The #34's whole law (the grain steamed over the stew, the broth worked in at each of the three steamings) carries; the stew below is the osban's own simmer, and the grain's perfume is the parcels' own. - **The bridge:** the two master records carry their crafts' every bridge; the assembly's own work is the platter's — and the celebration's timing: the osban made through the morning, the couscous's steamings through the afternoon, the table at the gathering's hour.

Couscous with Osban

Prep: 15 min · Cook: 50 min · Total: 1 h 05 min · Serves 6

Ingredients

Ingredients

  • One batch of the #54's osban (about 8 parcels, cooked and sliced thick) — or the honest smaller path: the #54's half-batch (4 parcels)
  • One batch of the #34's couscous (500 g grain, the three steamings over the osban's own simmering broth — the two-story's marriage, whole)
  • The osban's simmering broth, reserved and strained (about 500 ml)
  • 100 g chickpeas, soaked and simmered in the osban's pot (the celebration's full table)
  • The service: the #105 mechouia's sharp bite (about 150 g), the #91 harissa thinned (about 30 g), lemon wedges, and the #119 mint tea to close

Instructions

  1. **The osban's simmer, per the #54** — the parcels' gentle hour in the seasoned water, the chickpeas joining the pot's broth, the mosaic's proof at the test parcel's cut. Checkpoint — the #54's own: the center's swollen-tender rice, the tripe's soft-firm sheath — the parcels lifted, the broth strained and reserved for the grain's steamings.
  2. **The couscous's three steamings, per the #34** — the grain worked and steamed over the osban's broth, thrice, the broth's ladle worked in at each turning. Checkpoint — the #34's own: the grain distinct, perfumed, twice-swollen — the osban's own savor run through every pearl.
  3. **The platter — the celebration's assembly.** The couscous mounded to the great platter's center, a broth-ladle worked through; the sliced osban fanned in the crown — each slice's mosaic-face up, the celebration's own presentation — the chickpeas scattered through, the mechouia and the harissa at the table's edge. Checkpoint — eating test, from the shared platter: the grain's osban-perfumed lightness under the slice's mosaic — the rice's herbs and the liver's depth, the tripe's soft chew — the broth's own savor in every spoonful, the mechouia's fire cutting the richness. It should taste like the celebration's whole argument: the kitchen's longest craft and the canon's staple, one platter, and the assembly's own blessing.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
See the masters' tablesThe two crafts' lawsThe #54's and the #34's rows carry
The platter's grain dryThe broth's ladle shy at the steamingsThe #34's own law — three ladles, three steamings

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- The osban and the grain keep per their masters (the osban's fried revival the finest second day); the assembled platter is the table's own hour. - Variations: the #25 mombar's substitution (the sister craft's parcels), the dfina's beef over the grain (#56's own service). The masters carry; the platter's dial turns.
